memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'By each stack put some pure incense as a memorial portion to
represent the bread and to be a food offering presented to the LORD'"
- Lev 24:7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Alongside the bread sat pure incense, described as a memorial portion.
The bread stayed on the table; the incense rose. It was a fragrant
reminder before God of the people the loaves represented.

Of course God does not need reminding. He forgets nothing. The
arrangement was for Israel's sake — a visible, physical assurance that
their God held them in mind.

Dear friend, the New Testament picks up this imagery beautifully. When
Cornelius prayed and gave to the poor, the angel told him that his
prayers and gifts had come up as a memorial offering before God (Acts
10:4). John saw golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of
God's people (Rev 5:8).

Do you see what that means for your prayer life? Your prayers are not
lost in the air. They are not evaporating against a closed ceiling.
Scripture pictures them as fragrance rising and received in heaven.

Paul says the life poured out in love is like a fragrant offering
(Eph 5:2). Even your quiet, stumbling, half-finished prayers matter.

If you have been praying for years with no visible answer, take heart.
The incense is still rising. God has not stopped receiving it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I believe my prayers actually reach God and are received?
2. What long-standing prayer have I been tempted to abandon?
3. How would I pray differently if I truly pictured incense rising?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that my prayers rise before You like fragrance and
are never wasted. Give me faith to keep praying, especially where I see
no answer yet. Amen.
